title: Mistaken arrest near Zanesville
summary: A pianist robbed a post office and armed police detained the band at gunpoint until a boy identified him.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: All right, where we at, now? Three Deuces. Right?
Well, no.
Oh, right.
Buckeye Lake.

Right. So on the way there we stopped in this gas station, I guess about ten miles out of Zanesville. And I had to get some gas. It was also a sub post office. Now, the only thing that saved us was that there was a little boy that had seen Gabby take the money. He drank the soda down, then he reached in the till and took out this bread -- unbeknownst to us, you know. But it looked like a set-up, you know.
So as we were... I got the gas to put in, you know; the
Eldridge - 111

car was running beautifully. And then, WHOO-OO, WHOO-OO, police cars were going, and I said, "There must have been an accident somewhere." They was going to see what happened, you know; but we didn't know this. So just as we pulled out the town, a car pulled over and throws me into the curb. And I went to get out of my car, I went to reach for my license, because I thought I was speeding -- and the guy put a big Winchester right at my head, man. And I turned around in circles, and... They had other guys with machine guns. T they were heavily armed. So I couldn't figure it out. I said, "For speeding?" to myself. I said, "What's the trouble, officer, sir?" The guy said, "Don't talk." He said, "Just shut up, because I'm nervous. I'm gonna shoot and talk later." " So I said, I'd better keep my mouth shut, you know.

So a crowd gathered around, and I couldn't get no explanation for what had happened. Plus, we had a jar full of pot all rolled pretty for our trip back to New York, and I think, "Well, this is it for sure." They put us in the patrol car. And I said, "Well, what about my car?" He said, "Don't worry. We're going to search your car." I said, "That's it," you know.
In the meantime, Gabby(?) is trying to get in his pocket, and he was handcuffed to a truck. I think Joe and
Eldridge - 112
Billy Bowen had gone ahead, because Billy had his car, you know.

So they carried us down there, and when we got in the courthouse, where the jail was and everything, I seen this little boy. I said, "Oh, man, this is ...(?)... that got the soda." So they brought us all in there, and we were sitting down, and the little boy come out and pointed at Gabby -- so Gabby was the only one they took away.

And the man came back, and he called me... He talked to the other guys first. He said, "You're the leader, right?" I said, "Yeah." He said, "Did you pay your guys last night?" I said, "Yeah." He said, "Well, how much money would you say your piano had?" I said, "I know what he had. I know what I gave him last night. When we checked out, he couldn't have no more than (?)." So he said, "Well, it's too bad, because he just robbed the Post Office." I said, "What?!"

And my band, like... It was John Collins, Harold West, Gabby(?), Chuck and myself. Well, the four of us wanted... thought, "Please put us in the cell with him" -- because we was guilty! Now I'm worried about the car, right? So I said, "Well, we didn't know anything about that." He said, "I know, he went in there, and the only thing that saved you guys was that the little boy seen him take it, and he knew
Eldridge - 113
which one took it."

So he said, "Now, let me ask you something"... No, I asked him, "Let me ask you something. How come you were shaking when you were holding that big Winchester rifle on me?" He said, "Well, some people came through here from Chicago once before, and one of our men got shot." Remember I told you I went to reach in my pocket to get my license?" It's a wonder he hadn't shot me then. He said, "So I was nervous and wasn't taking no chances."

Now, we had to stay there. They didn't search the car, see. That's all they were looking for, you know. Oh, was I relieved! So we had to stay there for about two hours while they notified all the sheriffs all the way to Ohio, because it was on the pipeline, on the air, you know, that we were free and clear, that we were coming through, so that we wouldn't get stopped again.

And you should have seen the headlines. "Six Burly Negroes Rob Post Office." No, "Heavily (?) at the edge of town by policemen, heavily armed." I wish I had that right up there. It did have it for years, but I don't know what the hell happened to it. So that was that.
So you arrived without a piano player.
Yeah. Then we got Clyde to play with us. Clyde Hart. Heh-heh-heh... Oh, boy.
